_doc: THE ENGRAVING RULES — LGMF PLAN 2e (planned 2026-09-27, RUNNING_LOG §408 … §447; built from §448). Every placement and style rule of the notation lives HERE, in five tables, each row with its `basis` (lilypond · gould · composer §N · AI §N · census) and its `ref` (the § or the day that decided it). The devices and the look blocks of container.json POINT at these rows ("@objects.cueHead.size"); notation/lib/rules.js compiles the pointers into the registry keys the layout and the renderer read, and throws on a pointer with no row. docs/ENGRAVING_RULES.md is GENERATED from this file (tools/gen_engraving_rules.js) — never hand-edit it. tools/check_rules.js holds the gates. THE FIVE LAYERS (§413, his 'yes'): (1) THE ANCHOR — which point of a unit sits on x(t) · (2) THE COLUMN — the order and the side of what stacks on a unit · (3) THE OBJECTS — one row per drawn object type, four distances in ss (`parent` to what it hangs on · `staff` the floor from the staff edge · `stack` to the next stacked mark · `beside` horizontal) + face · size · colour · (4) THE PAGE — page_rules.json `edge` (not here: one table per file) · (5) THE EXCEPTIONS — the ladder. A value marked `census` is what drew on 2026-09-27 when the tables were built (2e.1, a re-housing: every page byte-identical); a later decision changes the ROW, with its §, and the page follows.

anchors._doc: LAYER 1 — THE ANCHOR (§414 · §416 · §418): which point of a unit sits on x(t). The principle, gated (check_rules 6): the head ON its time ↔ no go line; a go line ↔ the head off its time. G metric (a passage not spaced by time) is a HELD candidate (§416), not a row. `gapSs` = the distance from x(t) to the unit's near ink edge; `justify` the side of x(t) the unit sits on; `regime` the column's regime (HUG — every member on the head side, mirrored with the stem · ROWS — the dynamic on the dynamic row, text above); `columnAlign` how the column rows align on the unit.

The floor tiers (§424 · §425): the staccato dot and the tenuto line may sit inside the staff, in a SPACE, never on a line; every other mark outside the staff by its own `staff` distance. `rows` are the fixed rows in ss from the middle line (+ up).

objects._doc: LAYER 3 — THE OBJECTS (§421 · §422 · §427 · §428): one row per drawn object type. FOUR DISTANCES in ss — `parent` to what it hangs on · `staff` the floor from the staff edge · `stack` to the next stacked mark · `beside` horizontal — and a FIFTH (2h.1, §474, his 2g.6 eye): `after`, the horizontal clearance a time-spanning object keeps between its END and the leftmost ink of the next unit. `face` · `size` (ss for text, a scale for a glyph) · `colour` (a key of `colours`). `draws` names the layout's item kinds this row covers (`kind` or `glyph:<name pattern>` or `anim:<kind>` or `kind[seq]`) — gate (2): a drawn kind with no row fails the build. `variantOf` marks a row that draws with another row's glyph at its own size. His approved numbers are kept; anything undecided is seeded from LilyPond 2.24.4's define-grobs.scm on his machine (§422) — a seed is marked basis lilypond. New sizes are chosen on LilyPond's step 2^(1/6) (§428). `in` names where a value that is not compiled still lives (glyphs.json standards, a code literal) — the census of §448. 'leaves' (§458, his (a)): the order a mark leaves the head side when the ladder flips — 1 the ANNOTATION (the words and the symbols; the default for a row without the field), 2 the PITCH DATA (the cents and the partial), which stays with the head until nothing else helps.

pitchPicture._doc: THE PITCH PICTURE OF A JUST NOTE (docs/research/just_partials_notation.md §1a, REVISED 2026-09-27): the accidental shows the NEAREST point on the quarter-tone grid — |cents| < edgeCents → the plain accidental of the tempered spelling · ≥ edgeCents → a quarter-tone sign; no arrows (the six arrowed glyphs stay baked in glyphs.json, unused). THE SPELLING: the origin is the nearest tempered pitch (|cents| ≤ 50); a quarter-tone sign points from the origin toward the truth, so a sharp-side deviation is spelled with a natural or a sharp (½♯ · ¾♯) and a flat-side one with a natural or a flat (the reversed flat · ¾♭): D♯ +41 is D¾♯ +41, D♯ −41 is E¾♭ −41, never E¼♭ / D¼♯. The picture is taken in the realization's WRITTEN pitch; the cents and the partial never change with it.
pitchPicture.ref: §432 · §435 (the nearest quarter-tone, nothing finer — his) · §433 (the spelling: the tuner's origin) · §436 (no arrows)

techniqueChange._doc: THE VIBRATO WORDS (§443 · §445, LG-115; the shape of #5 D52's dynamics-on-change): per part, in time order, over the notes whose technique is one of `texts` — at a note whose technique differs from the part's last such technique, its word is written (once per change per part); the part's FIRST `senza_vel` note carries "senza vib." (the piece's first), an `ord` note carries "ord." only after a senza passage (`firstAlso` lists the techniques written at a part's first note). The word goes into the sequence block's column when the note opens a block, else an instruction on the note's part at its time. The rule fires only where the save has it: the SI2 players' `ord` (their library's plain sustain, never after a senza note) writes nothing.

vibMarks._doc: THE VIBRAPHONE'S MARKS IN A SEQUENCE (PLAN 2g — §463 · §465 · §466; LG-116, his: 'hairpins describe dynamic movement and direction. The dynamic markings describe a relative level'): notation/lib/vib_marks.js reads each bow's slice of its seat's level curve into names and TIMED hairpins, tied to the BOW. The level = sequence_overlays.js writtenAt (the body through the part's ladder × the fade weight, §462 · §465) in written steps (0 ppp … 7 fff, −1 niente). A LEG (a monotone run between the turning points, the flats ignored) of ≥ hairpinSteps draws a hairpin; of nameSteps … hairpinSteps only when its rounded end name differs from the current name; under flatSteps nothing. A name at a leg's end where the rounded level differs from the current name, at the time reached (a plateau's start). No name without a hairpin, no hairpin without motion. `carry`: a bow's start name is its chain's previous bow's END name, never re-rounded — re-read from the level only at the chain's first bow and after a rest of ≥ restS. A bow whose fade rises from 0 opens with the niente circle in place of its start name; the fade-out ends at the level reached (the circle at 0). `repeatName` false: a flat bow at the carried level draws nothing. `flip` false: a voice's row is meaning — the ladder never flips these marks. minHairpinSs: a hairpin shorter than this between its marks is dropped, the names stand. The voice of a bow: `voice`.
vibMarks.voice: by register: a bow is UPPER when its pitch is ≥ the other chain's sounding pitch at the bow's start; a silent partner → the nearer of its previous and next bow in the same sequence; a tie → chain 0 upper; no partner in the sequence → chain 0 upper
vibMarks.ref: §463 rules 1 … 7 (his '1 numbers good, 1-6 good': the thresholds 0.5 · 0.25 · 0.25 · the carry · his (a), the repeated name left off) · §465 (the fades timed; the level read WITH the fade) · §466 — the AI's, his to reverse at 2g.6: flip false · minHairpinSs 1 · restS 0.5 (#4's breathSeconds) · the voice rule; the plan's `hairpinStepSs` · `nameStepSs` · `flatStepSs` are named `…Steps` here — they are written steps, not staff spaces

ladder._doc: LAYER 5 — THE EXCEPTIONS: LADDER v2 (§422 · §423), BUILT at 2e.4 (RUNNING_LOG §451): notation/lib/fit.js runs it per unit in the layout (the frame's lane boxes in ss, from the caller), THE WALK (§458, his (a)): 1 compress · 3 flip the annotation ('leaves' 1) · 2 shrink · 3 flip the pitch data ('leaves' 2) — the numbers name the KIND of move, the rungs array is the ORDER; 4 … 7 page-level (not automatic), 8 manual; the rung reached is written on the moved items (`fit: { rung, by }`) and on the model's report (`model.fit`); a unit that fits is never touched. Rung 8 is an override ON THE EVENT — an `engraving` overlay { rung: 8, object, property (dySs · dxSs · size), value, ref } — never in code, never prose-only; until it exists the unit is marked red on the page and listed by tools/decisions_needed.js (and notate_section's build output); the same override recurring is the promotion signal. `built` switches it (compiled into engraving.layout.ladder.on).
